patient.chief_complaint: Known GRN mutation carrier — behavioral concerns at age 59; son reports behavioral changes over past 10 months
patient.history_present_illness: Ms. P is a 59-year-old retired pharmacist who is a known carrier of a pathogenic GRN splice site mutation (c.709-1G>A), identified 2 years ago through cascade family genetic testing after her daughter was diagnosed with early-onset FTD-GRN at age 34. Her mother died of dementia at age 62, retrospectively consistent with FTD. Her brother, also a carrier, is currently asymptomatic at age 61. She presents today with her son, who has been increasingly concerned about behavioral changes over the past 10 months. She is aware of her genetic status and is actively monitoring herself for symptom onset. She retired from pharmacy 2 years ago, partly precipitated by her daughter's diagnosis. Her son describes a pattern that he initially attributed to grief and caregiver stress related to her daughter's illness. However, over the past several months, he has noted behaviors that concern him: she has been making repetitive errors in managing her daughter's complex medication schedule — forgetting steps she herself established — and then insisting she completed them. She has become emotionally blunted in a way her son finds striking — she does not visibly grieve her daughter's deteriorating condition. She recently gave away a collection of her daughter's childhood photographs without discussing it with any family members, causing significant family distress. She has developed a highly rigid daily routine and becomes irritable when it is disrupted. She has stopped calling her friends of 30+ years. She continues to function in basic ADLs and manages her own finances, but her son is concerned about subtle errors. The clinical challenge is determining whether these changes represent early symptomatic bvFTD-GRN or are within the range of grief and adjustment reactions in a high-stress caregiver who knows she carries a dementia gene. GRN-FTD has specific features: typically asymmetric (often left-sided), can present with CBS features (alien hand, apraxia), earlier age of onset than sporadic FTD, and low plasma progranulin level as a biomarker.

results.title: Anti-sortilin antibody AL001 increases plasma progranulin in GRN mutation carriers

output.summary: GRN-FTD is caused by haploinsufficiency (50% reduction in progranulin). Disease-modifying strategies aim to increase progranulin levels: (1) Latozinemab (anti-sortilin antibody) — sortilin promotes progranulin degradation; blocking sortilin increases progranulin. INFRONT-3 Phase 3 trial showed attenuation of CSF NfL increase (biomarker of neurodegeneration) in GRN-FTD. (2) Gene therapy approaches are in clinical trials. GRN mutation carriers may be eligible for specialized FTD research center enrollment and targeted therapeutic trials.

results.title: Genetic counseling in familial FTD: GRN, C9orf72, and MAPT

output.summary: GRN pathogenic mutations follow autosomal dominant inheritance — each first-degree relative of a GRN mutation carrier has a 50% chance of inheriting the mutation. Key clinical steps: (1) all first-degree relatives should be offered genetic counseling and testing; (2) presymptomatic carriers benefit from neuroimaging and biomarker monitoring; (3) plasma progranulin is a non-invasive screening biomarker — GRN carriers have ~50% reduction; (4) enrollment in natural history studies and clinical trials should be offered to all symptomatic and presymptomatic carriers. Clinical correlation recommended.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia — GRN (progranulin) pathogenic variant (c.709-1G>A) — FTLD-TDP type A pathology — presenting with combined bvFTD and early corticobasal syndrome features

differential.key_features: Structural left frontoparietal atrophy on MRI, low plasma progranulin (42 ng/mL), elevated CSF NfL, left frontoparietal FDG-PET hypometabolism — all confirm active neurodegeneration, not reactive behavioral changes
Amyloid PET negative — CBS can be caused by AD pathology (in which case amyloid PET would be positive). Negative amyloid PET confirms FTLD-TDP pathology consistent with GRN mutation.
Pathogenic GRN splice site mutation confirmed; low plasma progranulin; family history consistent with autosomal dominant FTD-GRN
No supranuclear gaze palsy, no falls, no midbrain atrophy — GRN mutations can rarely cause PSP-syndrome but pattern here is CBS/bvFTD not PSP

critical_actions: Plasma progranulin is a disease-specific biomarker for GRN-FTD — should be checked in all GRN carriers to confirm haploinsufficiency
Amyloid PET must be obtained when CBS features are present — CBS can be caused by AD pathology, which requires different management
Refer to specialized FTD research center for clinical trial enrollment — GRN-FTD is the most advanced in targeted therapy pipeline (latozinemab)
contraindicated_actions: Attributing behavioral changes to grief without structural/biomarker assessment in a known GRN carrier at peak risk age
key_reasoning_points: GRN-FTD is caused by haploinsufficiency — plasma progranulin level is a direct biomarker of disease-related biology; level <60 ng/mL in a GRN mutation carrier confirms active disease

GRN-FTD characteristically shows ASYMMETRIC frontoparietal atrophy (often left-sided) — different from the more symmetric frontal pattern of C9orf72-FTD or sporadic bvFTD; this asymmetry can produce CBS features
When CBS features are present, amyloid PET is mandatory — CBS is caused by FTLD-TDP (GRN mutations) OR by Alzheimer's disease pathology; these require different treatment approaches
GRN-FTD is entering the era of targeted therapy — latozinemab (anti-sortilin antibody) is the first disease-modifying candidate; clinical trial referral should be standard of care for GRN carriers
